pass: The LOCAL half of the wrong-person class -- chairs built from a different politician's evidence. The federal half closed in migration 1896 / ev-accounts #904; this is what it left behind, re-read person by person rather than key by key.
headline: The handoff recorded 8 rows across 5 officials plus 2 candidates. Read as PEOPLE rather than as keys it is 27 rows across 6 officials -- and the 2 candidates were not defects at all. 24 keys blanked, 3 blocked, 2 recorded findings withdrawn.
the_lesson: A BORROWED BILL CITATION IS WORSE THAN A BORROWED CAMPAIGN WEBSITE. Migration 1896 found that a borrowed campaign site scores clean on every "is this generic?" test. The local rows go one level deeper: Ortega's and Bennett's contaminated chairs cite leginfo.legislature.ca.gov BILL PAGES -- the most specific, most primary-looking source in the corpus -- and the bills are real. They are simply SOMEONE ELSE'S BILLS. Only the rows that happened to cite a Wikipedia biography were visible to the probe that found them, and those were the minority.

three_distinct_mechanisms.1_succession_link: Steve Bennett <- Suzette Martinez Valladares. Her article names him EXACTLY ONCE, in the infobox line "Member of the California State Assembly from the 38th district ... Succeeded by Steve Bennett". The predecessor's article is one click from the subject's own and names him as his own predecessor. This is not a name collision and no name-based probe can find it -- every officeholder has such a neighbour.
three_distinct_mechanisms.2_inheritance_from_a_mentor: Katy Yaroslavsky <- Sheila Kuehl. Not a misfiling at all: the research states the gap in its own words ("No specific vote or statement on childcare policy was found") and then seats the chair on the county supervisor she once worked for. Every name on the page is correct, so no name-token, state or party probe can see it. Whom someone worked for is not a position they hold.
three_distinct_mechanisms.3_invented_party_and_invented_instrument: Steve Johnson (MD, Democrat). All eight chairs at rung 4, each reached by calling him a Republican, while his own cited page says "Party Democrat". Five of the eight rest on bills absent from the 150 his page lists, and one claim is contradicted outright: the row says he opposes "major police accountability reforms" and his page lists him as a CO-SPONSOR of HB0508, Public Safety - Police Accountability - Investigation Records.

proof_from_our_own_corpus: The strongest proof needed no external page. Laura Richardson and Suzette Martinez Valladares are both rows in this database, both CALIFORNIA STATE SENATORS, and our own rows for them attribute the very same bills to them. "Richardson authored SB 510 (2025)" and "Authored SB 510" sit in the corpus under two different people; so do SB 530, SB 611, SB 752, SB 767, SB 34, SB 1137 and SB 1144. Liz Ortega is an Assembly Member credited with authoring SENATE bills and with a "prior US House record" she does not have; Steve Bennett is a Democratic Assembly member described as a "Republican senator".

withdrawn_false_positives.finding: WRONG. jasmineforok.com IS her own campaign site; she campaigns under her middle name. The page is headed "N'kiyla Jasmine Thomas For US Senate" and its footer reads "Paid for By N'Kiyla For OK". Her 7 Season 1 and 2 Season 2 rows are sound and were left alone.

WRONG. The cited WWNO candidate Q&A names him 5 times, runs his photo, and carries his answers in the first person -- "I am Moderate/pro-choice. I support legal abortion in some circumstances. I oppose total abortion bans ... totally against 3rd trimester abortions unless the woman's life is in jeopardy", which is exactly the chair his row holds (3). Both his rows are sound.

why_both_were_wrong: The probe behind them -- "does any source name them?" -- was run against the URL and the name string, not against the PAGE. A probe that FIRES must be confirmed by reading the page, exactly as a probe that is SILENT must be confirmed with a control term. Otherwise it manufactures false defects as readily as it finds real ones.

method_notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval even with a browser User-Agent; legiscan.com likewise. Their contents are NOT asserted in either direction. The bill-authorship proof comes from this database's own rows for Richardson and Valladares.
openstates.org is JS-rendered -- it returns 53 bytes of "You need to enable JavaScript to run this app." A control term caught it. Nothing is asserted from it. Same trap as GovTrack in 1896.
ballotpedia.org/Steve_Johnson_(Maryland) returned HTTP 200 with EVERY control term at 0, including both party names. A 200 is not a read. Recorded as NOT READ.

The MGA member page lists the 2025 and 2026 sessions only, so absence of a bill is established for that window and NOT for 2023-2024 -- except the SAVE Our Elections Act of 2026, which is dated inside it. The limit is written into every Johnson blank rather than left implicit.

Re-running probe 2 after migration 1896 returns 39 rows rather than 27, because 1896's OWN BLANKS carry the contaminated URLs as "sources examined". Explaining a defect in prose makes you a permanent false positive -- the same effect recorded for migration 1882.
